Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ever adverb

at any time

also at any time, have you ever, if ever, hardly ever, ever since

classical

Cic. Fam. 14.3.5: nec umquam fuisse
Ter. Eun. 852: sī aliam admīserō umquam, occīditō
Plin. Ep. 5.16.1: nihil umquam fēstīvius
Traupman 311

umquam (unquam)

adverb; mostly after a negative, in conditions and in questions · Wiktionary

ever, at any time

“Never” is numquam, and “not … ever” nec umquam, nēmō umquam. “Ever since” is ex quō or ūsque ab (Traupman 379).

Other words

  • 1aliquandō: long final o (Lewis & Short aliquandŏ). A compound of quandō, which de Vaan gives with a long final vowel (p. 507, s.v. quī); Festus records an older form quandōd (Lewis & Short s.v. quando). The Latinitas loci write aliquandō throughout, and the libellī quandō.

    aliquandō1 — ever (asking about a time not fixed); at some time

    adverb · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 8.8.1: vīdistīne aliquandō Clitumnum fontem?; Sen. Ep. 72.8: vīdistī aliquandō canem …? · Wiktionary

    Where umquam belongs to denials and doubt, aliquandō belongs to plain statements and open questions (Lewis & Short).

  • quandō — ever (after sī, nisi, nē, num)

    indefinite adverb: sī quandō, if ever · also used · classical · Mor. 67: sī quandō vacuum casula pluviaeve tenēbant; Catull. 84.1: sī quandō commoda vellet dīcere · Wiktionary

Examples

  • cūrā ut valeās et ita tibi persuādeās, mihi tē cārius nihil esse nec umquam fuisse

    look after yourself, and be sure that nothing is or ever was dearer to me than youCic. Fam. 14.3.5

  • vīdistīne aliquandō Clitumnum fontem?

    have you ever seen the spring of Clitumnus?Plin. Ep. 8.8.1

  • Ūnam hanc noxiam mitte: sī aliam admīserō umquam, occīditō.

    Let this one fault go: if I ever do another, kill me.Ter. Eun. 851–852

See also once, sometimes.
